title.zh: 卷269 列傳五十六 索额图 明珠
title.en: Volume 269 Biographies 56: Suo Etu, Ming Zhu
title.raw: 卷269 列傳五十六 索额图 明珠

sentences.zh: 索額圖明珠余國柱佛倫

translations.literal: Songgotu, Mingzhu, Yu Guozhu, and Folun
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu, Mingzhu, Yu Guozhu, and Folun

sentences.zh: 索額圖，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人，索尼第二子。

translations.literal: Songgotu, of the Heseri clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and the second son of Sony.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu of the Heseri clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was Sony's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛，自三等洊升一等。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a guard, and was promoted step by step from third to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a guard and rose in steady steps from third to first rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed vice president of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 (1668) he became vice president of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，自請解任效力左右，復為一等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he asked to resign his post and serve at the emperor's side, and was again made a first-rank guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 8 (1669) he resigned his office to serve at court and was restored to first-rank guard.

sentences.zh: 及鼇拜獲罪，大學士班布爾善坐黨誅，授索額圖國史院大學士，兼佐領。

translations.literal: When Oboi was condemned, Grand Secretary Banbursan was executed for partisan attachment; Songgotu was appointed grand secretary of the Historiographic Institute and concurrently made a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Oboi's fall, Grand Secretary Banbursan was put to death as his partisan; Songgotu was made grand secretary of the Historiographic Institute and company commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，改保和殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to be grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 (1670) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 十一年，世祖實錄成，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor were completed, he was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672), on completion of the Shunzhi Veritable Records, he received the title Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大學士熊賜履票本有誤，改寫草簽，既又毀去。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü's draft memorial contained an error; he rewrote it on a slip and then destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 (1676) Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü's draft memorial was faulty; he rewrote it on a slip and then destroyed the slip.

sentences.zh: 索額圖與大學士巴泰、杜立德等疏劾，賜履坐罷歸。

translations.literal: Songgotu, together with Grand Secretaries Batai, Du Lide, and others, memorialized in impeachment, and Cilü was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu joined Grand Secretaries Batai and Du Lide in impeaching him, and Cilü was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，京察，侍講學士顧八代隨徵稱職，翰林院以「政勤才長」注考，索額圖改注「浮躁」，竟坐降調。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the metropolitan evaluation, Lecturing Reader Gu Badai was rated competent on the campaign circuit; the Hanlin Academy entered him as 'diligent in government and gifted in talent,' but Songgotu changed the entry to 'frivolous,' and he was in the end demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kangxi 18 (1679) metropolitan review, Lecturing Reader Gu Badai was rated competent on campaign service; the Hanlin entered 'diligent in government, gifted in talent,' but Songgotu altered it to 'frivolous,' and Badai was demoted.

sentences.zh: 語詳顧八代傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in the biography of Gu Badai.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Gu Badai's biography.

sentences.zh: 索額圖權勢日盛。

translations.literal: Songgotu's power and influence grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu's power grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 會地震，左都御史魏象樞入對，陳索額圖怙權貪縱狀，請嚴譴。

translations.literal: When an earthquake occurred, Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangsu came to audience and set forth Songgotu's abuse of power, greed, and license, asking for severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After an earthquake, Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangsu reported Songgotu's abuse of power, greed, and license, and urged severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「修省當自朕始！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Self-reform should begin with me!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Self-reform must begin with me!'

sentences.zh: 翌日，召索額圖及諸大臣諭曰：「茲遘地震，朕反躬修省。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Songgotu and the other ministers and instructed them: 'Now that we have met with earthquake, I turn inward in self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Songgotu and the ministers and said, 'This earthquake has come; I must examine myself.

sentences.zh: 爾等亦宜洗滌肺腸，公忠自矢。

translations.literal: You too should cleanse your hearts and pledge yourselves to public duty and loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: You too must cleanse your hearts and devote yourselves to the public good.

sentences.zh: 自任用後，諸臣家計頗皆饒裕，乃朋比徇私，益加貪黷。

translations.literal: Since you have been in office, the household means of many ministers have grown quite ample; yet you form factions for private ends and grow ever more corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Since your appointments, many of you have grown wealthy, yet you form factions for private ends and grow ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 若事情發覺，國法具在，決不爾貸！」

translations.literal: If matters come to light, the laws of the state stand ready—I will by no means spare you!'
translations.idiomatic: If your deeds are exposed, the law stands ready—I will not spare you!'

sentences.zh: 是時索額圖、明珠同柄朝政，互植私黨，貪侈傾朝右，故諭及之。

translations.literal: At this time Songgotu and Mingzhu together held the reins of government, each planting private factions; their greed and extravagance dominated the court, and so the admonition was directed at them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Songgotu and Mingzhu shared power, each building private factions; their greed and extravagance dominated the court, which is why he spoke as he did.

sentences.zh: 上並書「節制謹度」榜賜焉。

translations.literal: The emperor also wrote the words 'restraint and careful measure' on a placard and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wrote 'restraint and careful measure' on a placard and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，以病乞解任，上優旨獎其「勤敏練達，用兵以來，贊畫機宜」，改命為內大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year, on grounds of illness he asked to resign his post; the emperor with a gracious edict praised his 'diligence, quickness, and mastery, and since the opening of military operations his assistance in planning,' and reassigned him as interior minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kangxi 19 (1680) he resigned on grounds of illness; the emperor praised his diligence and skill in war planning and made him an interior minister.

sentences.zh: 尋授議政大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 先是索額圖兄噶布拉，以冊諡孝誠仁皇后推恩所生，封一等公；

translations.literal: Earlier Songgotu's elder brother Gabula, as a son born to whom favor was extended when Empress Xiaochengren was given her posthumous title, was enfeoffed as a first-rank duke;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Songgotu's elder brother Gabula had been enfeoffed as a first-rank duke when favor was extended to the empress's birth family at Xiaochengren's posthumous investiture;

sentences.zh: 弟心裕，襲索尼初封一等伯；

translations.literal: his younger brother Xinyu inherited Sony's original enfeoffment as a first-rank baron;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Xinyu inherited Sony's original rank as a first-rank baron;

sentences.zh: 法保，襲索尼加封一等公。

translations.literal: Fabao inherited Sony's augmented enfeoffment as a first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao inherited Sony's augmented rank as a first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 二十三年三月，以心裕等嬾惰驕縱，責索額圖弗能教，奪內大臣、議政大臣、太子太傅，但任佐領，並奪法保一等公。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year, because Xinyu and the others were idle, arrogant, and unrestrained, Songgotu was blamed for failing to instruct them; he was stripped of interior minister, deliberative minister, and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, retaining only company command, and Fabao's first-rank dukedom was also taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 23 (1684), Xinyu and the others were condemned as idle and arrogant; Songgotu was blamed for poor discipline, stripped of his ministerial posts and Grand Tutor title, left only as company commander, and Fabao lost his dukedom.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed senior interior minister of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 (1686) he was appointed senior interior minister of the guards.

sentences.zh: 時俄羅斯屢侵黑龍江邊境，據雅克薩，其眾去復來，上發兵圍之。

translations.literal: At this time Russia repeatedly encroached on the Amur frontier, occupied Albazin, and its people withdrew and returned; the emperor sent troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Russia had repeatedly raided the Amur frontier and held Albazin, its garrison withdrawing and returning; the emperor sent troops to besiege the post.

sentences.zh: 察罕汗謝罪，使費耀多囉等來議界。

translations.literal: The tsar apologized and sent Fyodor Alekseyevich and others to negotiate the border.
translations.idiomatic: The tsar apologized and sent Fyodor Alekseyevich and others to negotiate the boundary.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上命索額圖與都統佟國綱往議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor ordered Songgotu and Commander-in-Chief Tong Guogang to go and negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 (1689) the emperor sent Songgotu and Commander-in-Chief Tong Guogang to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 索額圖奏謂：「尼布楚、雅克薩兩地當歸我。」

translations.literal: Songgotu memorialized saying: 'Nerchinsk and Albazin, both places, ought to return to us.'
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu memorialized that Nerchinsk and Albazin ought both to remain Chinese territory.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「尼布楚歸我，則俄羅斯貿易無所棲止，可以額爾固納河為界。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'If Nerchinsk returns to us, Russia will have nowhere to lodge its trade; the Argun River may serve as the boundary.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that if Nerchinsk were kept, Russia would have no base for trade, and proposed the Argun River as the boundary.'

sentences.zh: 索額圖等與議，費耀多囉果執尼布楚、雅克薩為請。

translations.literal: Songgotu and the others negotiated; Fyodor Alekseyevich indeed insisted on Nerchinsk and Albazin as his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the talks Fyodor Alekseyevich pressed for Nerchinsk and Albazin.

sentences.zh: 索額圖等力斥之，仍宣上意，以額爾固納河及格爾必齊河為界，立碑而還。

translations.literal: Songgotu and the others forcefully rejected this, still proclaimed the emperor's intent, fixed the boundary at the Argun and Gorbi Rivers, erected a stele, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu and his party firmly rejected the demand, upheld the emperor's terms, set the boundary at the Argun and Gorbi Rivers, erected boundary markers, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，上以裕親王福全為大將軍，擊噶爾丹，命索額圖將盛京、吉林、科爾沁兵會於巴林，敗噶爾丹於烏闌布通。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the emperor appointed Prince Yu Fuquan grand general to attack Galdan and ordered Songgotu to lead troops from Mukden, Jilin, and the Khorchin to assemble at Bairin; Galdan was defeated at Ulan Butung.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 (1690) Prince Yu Fuquan was made grand general against Galdan; Songgotu led Mukden, Jilin, and Khorchin forces to Bairin and helped defeat Galdan at Ulan Butung.

sentences.zh: 以不窮追，鐫四級。

translations.literal: For failing to pursue to the end, four ranks were struck from his record.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted four ranks for not pursuing the enemy to the end.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上親征，率八旗前鋒、察哈爾四旗及漢軍綠旗兵前行，並命督火器營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the emperor on a personal campaign, leading the Eight Banners vanguard, the four Chahar banners, and Han Green Standard troops forward, and was also ordered to supervise the firearms corps.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 (1696) he joined the emperor's personal campaign, leading the Eight Banners vanguard, four Chahar banners, and Green Standard Han troops, and supervised the firearms corps.

sentences.zh: 大將軍費揚古自西路抵圖拉。

translations.literal: Grand General Fiyanggū advanced from the western route to Tüla.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Fiyanggū advanced along the western route to Tüla.

sentences.zh: 上駐克魯倫河，噶爾丹遁走。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at the Kerulen River; Galdan fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor encamped on the Kerulen while Galdan fled.

sentences.zh: 費揚古截擊之於昭莫多，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Fiyanggū intercepted him at Jao Modo and routed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Fiyanggū intercepted him at Jao Modo and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，上還幸寧夏，命索額圖督水驛，會噶爾丹死。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the emperor returned and visited Ningxia, ordering Songgotu to supervise the water courier stations; Galdan died at this time.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 36 (1697) the emperor returned to Ningxia and put Songgotu in charge of the water courier route; Galdan died about then.

sentences.zh: 敘功，复前所鐫級。

translations.literal: Merit was reviewed and the ranks previously struck from his record were restored.
translations.idiomatic: His service was rewarded and the four ranks previously taken were restored.

sentences.zh: 四十年九月，以老乞休，心裕代為領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fortieth year, on grounds of age he asked to retire; Xinyu replaced him as senior interior minister of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Kangxi 40 (1701) he retired on grounds of age; Xinyu succeeded him as senior interior minister of the guards.

sentences.zh: 索額圖事皇太子謹，皇太子漸失上意。

translations.literal: Songgotu served the crown prince with care, but the crown prince gradually lost the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu served the crown prince faithfully, yet the heir gradually fell from the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上閱河至德州，皇太子有疾，召索額圖自京師至德州侍疾。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the emperor inspected the rivers as far as Dezhou; the crown prince fell ill, and Songgotu was summoned from the capital to Dezhou to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 41 (1702), while the emperor inspected the rivers at Dezhou, the crown prince fell ill; Songgotu was summoned from Beijing to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 居月馀，皇太子疾愈，還京師。

translations.literal: After more than a month the crown prince recovered and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the heir recovered and they returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，心裕以虐斃家人奪官。

translations.literal: That year Xinyu was stripped of office for cruelly beating a household member to death.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xinyu lost his post for beating a servant to death.

sentences.zh: 四十二年五月，上命執索額圖，交宗人府拘禁，諭曰：「爾為大學士，以貪惡革退，後復起用，罔知愧悔。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the forty-second year the emperor ordered Songgotu seized and handed over to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement, instructing him: 'You were a grand secretary, dismissed for greed and wickedness, then employed again, yet you know no shame or repentance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 42 (1703) the emperor had Songgotu arrested and confined by the Imperial Clan Court, saying, 'You were a grand secretary, dismissed for greed and corruption, then reappointed, yet you show no shame.

sentences.zh: 爾家人訐爾，留內三年，朕意欲寬爾。

translations.literal: Your household members denounced you; you were kept within for three years, and I meant to treat you leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Your own people denounced you; you were kept in confinement three years while I meant to be lenient.

sentences.zh: 爾乃怙過不悛，結黨妄行，議論國事。

translations.literal: Yet you cling to your faults without reform, form factions and act recklessly, and discuss state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cling to your faults, form factions, act recklessly, and debate state affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇太子在德州，爾乘馬至中門始下，即此爾已應死。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was at Dezhou, you rode your horse to the middle gate before dismounting—for this alone you deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: At Dezhou you rode to the middle gate before dismounting—for that alone you deserved death.

sentences.zh: 爾所行事，任舉一端，無不當誅。

translations.literal: Of your deeds, take any single instance—none would not merit execution.
translations.idiomatic: Any single deed of yours would merit execution.

sentences.zh: ​​朕念爾原系大臣，心有不忍，姑貸爾死。」

translations.literal: Considering that you were once a minister, my heart cannot bear it—I spare your life for the present.'
translations.idiomatic: Remembering you were once a minister, I cannot bring myself to kill you—for now I spare your life.'

sentences.zh: 又命執索額圖諸子交心裕、法保拘禁，諭：「若別生事端，心裕、法保當族誅！」

translations.literal: He also ordered Songgotu's sons seized and handed to Xinyu and Fabao for confinement, instructing: 'If any further trouble arises, Xinyu and Fabao shall suffer extermination of their clans!'
translations.idiomatic: He also had Songgotu's sons confined under Xinyu and Fabao, warning, 'If further trouble arises, Xinyu and Fabao's entire clans shall die!'

sentences.zh: 諸臣黨附索額圖者，麻爾圖、額庫禮、溫代、邵甘、佟寶並命嚴錮，阿米達以老貸之。

translations.literal: Ministers who had joined Songgotu's faction—Ma'ertu, E'ekuli, Wendai, Shao Gan, and Tong Bao—were all ordered strictly confined; Amida was spared on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu's partisans Ma'ertu, E'ekuli, Wendai, Shao Gan, and Tong Bao were strictly confined; Amida was spared because of his age.

sentences.zh: 又命諸臣同祖子孫在部院者，皆奪官。

translations.literal: He also ordered that all descendants of the same ancestral line serving in the ministries and courts be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: All their kinsmen serving in the ministries and courts were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 江潢以家有索額圖私書，下刑部論死。

translations.literal: Jiang Huang, because his household held private letters of Songgotu, was sent to the Ministry of Justice and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Huang was sent to the Ministry of Justice for execution because private letters from Songgotu were found in his home.

sentences.zh: 仍諭滿洲人與偶有來往者，漢官與交結者，皆貸不問。

translations.literal: He still instructed that Manchus who had had occasional contact and Han officials who had associated with him were all to be spared and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Manchus who had had only occasional contact and Han officials who had associated with him were spared and not questioned.

sentences.zh: 尋索額圖死於幽所。

translations.literal: Before long Songgotu died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Songgotu died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 後數年，皇太子以狂疾廢，上宣諭罪狀，謂：「索額圖助允礽潛謀大事，朕知其情，將索額圖處死。

translations.literal: Several years later the crown prince was deposed for madness; the emperor proclaimed his offenses, saying: 'Songgotu aided Yinreng in secretly plotting great matters; I knew the facts and was about to put Songgotu to death.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the crown prince was deposed for madness; the emperor announced his crimes, saying, 'Songgotu helped Yinreng plot treason; I knew it and was about to execute Songgotu.

sentences.zh: 今允礽欲為索額圖報仇，令朕戒慎不寧。」

translations.literal: Now Yinreng wishes to avenge Songgotu, keeping me vigilant and uneasy.'
translations.idiomatic: Now Yinreng seeks to avenge Songgotu, leaving me watchful and uneasy.'

sentences.zh: 並按誅索額圖二子格爾芬、阿爾吉善。

translations.literal: He also had Songgotu's two sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He also executed Songgotu's sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂廷臣曰：「昔索額圖懷私，倡議皇太子服禦俱用黃色，一切儀制幾與朕相似。

translations.literal: On another day the emperor told the court ministers: 'Formerly Songgotu, with private motives, proposed that the crown prince's dress and equipage all use yellow, and that every ritual form nearly resemble my own.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor told the court, 'Songgotu once urged that the crown prince's dress and regalia all be yellow, so that his ritual forms nearly matched my own.

sentences.zh: 驕縱之漸，實由於此。

translations.literal: The gradual growth of arrogance and license truly arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's growing arrogance truly began here.

sentences.zh: 索額圖誠本朝第一罪人也！」

translations.literal: Songgotu was truly this dynasty's foremost criminal!'
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was truly the greatest criminal of our dynasty!'

sentences.zh: 明珠，字端範，納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人，葉赫貝勒金台石孫。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, style name Duanfan, of the Nara clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and grandson of Yehe beile Gintaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu, styled Duanfan, of the Nara clan and the Bordered Yellow Banner, was a grandson of Yehe beile Gintaisi.

sentences.zh: 父尼雅哈，當太祖滅葉赫，來降，授佐領。

translations.literal: His father Niyaha, when the Taizu Emperor destroyed Yehe, came over in submission and was appointed a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Niyaha submitted when the Taizu destroyed Yehe and was made a company commander.

sentences.zh: 明珠自侍衛授鑾儀衛治儀正，遷內務府郎中。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, from guard service, was appointed director of ceremonial regulation in the Imperial Procession Guard and was transferred to be a director in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: From the guards Mingzhu became director of ceremonial regulation in the Imperial Procession Guard, then director in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，擢總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was promoted to superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664) he was promoted to superintendent.

sentences.zh: 五年，授弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 (1666) he became an academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 七年，命閱淮、揚河工，議復興化白駒場舊閘，鑿黃河北岸引河。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the Huai and Yangzhou river works, and proposed restoring the old sluice at Xinghua Baijuchang and cutting a diversion canal on the north bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 (1668) he inspected the Huai and Yangzhou river works and proposed restoring the Xinghua Baijuchang sluice and cutting a diversion on the Yellow River's north bank.

sentences.zh: 旋授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 改都察院左都御史，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be left censor-in-chief of the Censorate and served as a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He became left censor-in-chief of the Censorate and lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672) he became minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上幸南苑，閱八旗甲兵於晾鷹台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and reviewed the armored troops of the Eight Banners at the Hawk-Drying Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673) the emperor reviewed the Eight Banners armored troops at the Hawk-Drying Terrace in the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 明珠先布條教使練習之，及期，軍容整肅，上嘉其能，因著為令。

translations.literal: Mingzhu first laid down regulations and had them practiced; when the day came, the army's bearing was orderly and stern; the emperor praised his ability and made it a standing order.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu drew up drill regulations in advance; on the day of review the troops were perfectly ordered, and the emperor praised him and made his methods standard.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，南疆大定，留重兵鎮之：吳三桂雲南，尚可喜廣東，耿精忠福建。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi the south was largely pacified, and heavy garrisons were left to hold it: Wu Sangui in Yunnan, Shang Kexi in Guangdong, and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign the south was pacified but heavily garrisoned: Wu Sangui in Yunnan, Shang Kexi in Guangdong, and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十馀年，漸跋扈，三桂尤驕縱。

translations.literal: After more than ten years they grew gradually overbearing; Sangui was especially arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade they grew arrogant and overbearing, Sangui most of all.

sentences.zh: 可喜亦憂之，疏請撤籓，歸老海城。

translations.literal: Kexi too was troubled by this and memorialized asking that his fief be abolished and that he retire to old age at Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi too grew alarmed and memorialized to surrender his fief and retire to Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 精忠、三桂繼請。

translations.literal: Jingzhong and Sangui followed with similar requests.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong and Sangui soon made the same request.

sentences.zh: 上召諸大臣詢方略，戶部尚書米思翰、刑部尚書莫洛等主撤，明珠和之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the ministers to inquire about strategy; Minister of Revenue Misihan, Minister of Justice Moluo, and others advocated abolition, and Mingzhu agreed with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his ministers; Revenue Minister Misihan, Justice Minister Moluo, and others favored abolishing the fiefs, and Mingzhu agreed.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣皆默然。

translations.literal: The other ministers were all silent.
translations.idiomatic: The other ministers remained silent.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「三桂等蓄謀久，不早除之，將養癰成患。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Sangui and the others have long harbored designs; if we do not remove them early, we will nurse an abscess into a grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Sangui and the others have plotted for years; if we do not act now, we will nurse a sore into a mortal disease.

sentences.zh: 今日撤亦反，不撤亦反，不若先發。」

translations.literal: If we abolish the fiefs today they will rebel; if we do not abolish them they will rebel anyway—better to strike first.'
translations.idiomatic: Whether we abolish the fiefs or not they will rebel—better to strike first.'

sentences.zh: 因下詔許之。

translations.literal: He thereupon issued an edict granting permission.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict approving the plan.

sentences.zh: 三桂遂反，精忠及可喜子之信皆叛應之。

translations.literal: Sangui thereupon rebelled, and Jingzhong and Kexi's son Zhixin all rose in revolt in response.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui rebelled, and Jingzhong and Kexi's son Zhixin joined him.

sentences.zh: 時爭咎建議者，索額圖請誅之。

translations.literal: At the time blame was laid on those who had proposed the policy; Songgotu asked that they be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Blame fell on those who had urged abolition; Songgotu called for their execution.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此出自朕意，他人何罪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'This came from my own intent—what crime have others committed?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'This was my decision—what crime have the others committed?'

sentences.zh: 明珠由是稱上旨。

translations.literal: From this Mingzhu was said to have matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu was thereafter praised as having matched the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to be minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 (1675) he became minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授武英殿大學士，屢充實錄、方略、一統志、明史諸書總裁，累加太子太師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, repeatedly served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records, military annals, Comprehensive Gazetteer, and History of the Ming, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 (1677) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, repeatedly headed major compilations including the Veritable Records and History of the Ming, and rose to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 迨三叛既平，上諭廷臣以前議撤籓，惟明珠等能稱旨，且曰：「當時有請誅建議者，朕若從之，皆含冤泉壤矣！」

translations.literal: When the three rebellions had been pacified, the emperor told the court ministers that in the earlier debate on abolishing the fiefs only Mingzhu and others had matched his intent, and said: 'At the time some asked that those who had proposed it be put to death; had I followed them, all would lie wronged beneath the springs!'
translations.idiomatic: After the three rebellions were crushed, the emperor told the court that only Mingzhu and his allies had matched his intent on abolishing the fiefs, adding, 'Some then wanted the advocates executed; had I agreed, they would lie wronged in their graves!'

sentences.zh: 明珠既擅政，簠簋不飭，貨賄山積。

translations.literal: Once Mingzhu monopolized government, he was corrupt in office and bribes piled up like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingzhu dominated the government, he neglected official integrity and bribes piled mountain-high.

sentences.zh: 佛倫、餘國柱其黨也，援引致高位。

translations.literal: Folun and Yu Guozhu were his faction; he recommended and advanced them to high position.
translations.idiomatic: Folun and Yu Guozhu were his allies; he advanced them to high office.

sentences.zh: 靳輔督南河，主築堤束水，下游不濬自通。

translations.literal: Jin Fu supervised the southern rivers and advocated building dikes to confine the water, holding that the lower reaches need not be dredged and would clear of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu, supervising the southern rivers, favored dikes to confine the current, arguing the lower course need not be dredged.

sentences.zh: 於成龍等議濬下游，與異議。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong and others advocated dredging the lower reaches and differed in opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong and others urged dredging the lower reaches, and the two sides clashed.

sentences.zh: 輔興屯田，議者謂不便於民，多不右輔，明珠獨是其議。

translations.literal: Fu promoted military colonies; critics said they were inconvenient for the people, and most did not support Fu; only Mingzhu approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu also promoted military colonies; critics said they harmed the people, and most opposed him—only Mingzhu backed his plan.

sentences.zh: 蔡毓榮、張汧皆明珠所薦引者也，迨得罪按治，恐累舉者，傅輕比，上諭斥，始定。

translations.literal: Cai Yurong and Zhang Qian were both men Mingzhu had recommended and advanced; when they later offended and were prosecuted, fearing that their recommenders would be implicated, a lenient sentence was proposed; the emperor rebuked this and only then was the matter settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yurong and Zhang Qian had both been Mingzhu's protégés; when they were prosecuted, officials proposed leniency lest their patrons be implicated, until the emperor rebuked them and the sentences stood.

sentences.zh: 與索額圖互植黨相傾軋。

translations.literal: He and Songgotu each planted factions and undermined one another.
translations.idiomatic: He and Songgotu built rival factions and undermined each other.

sentences.zh: 索額圖生而貴盛，性倨肆，有不附己者顯斥之，於朝士獨親李光地。

translations.literal: Songgotu was born to wealth and eminence and was by nature arrogant and overbearing; those who did not attach themselves to him he openly rejected, and among court officials he was close only to Li Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Born to wealth and power, Songgotu was arrogant; he openly drove off those who would not join him and favored only Li Guangdi among the court.

sentences.zh: 明珠則務謙和，輕財好施，以招來新進，異己者以陰謀陷之，與徐乾學等相結。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, by contrast, cultivated humility and harmony, was free with money and fond of giving, to win over newcomers; those who differed from him he ruined by secret plots, and he allied with Xu Qianxue and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu cultivated humility, spent freely to win newcomers, ruined opponents by intrigue, and allied with Xu Qianxue and his circle.

sentences.zh: 索額圖善事皇太子，而明珠反之，朝士有侍皇太子者，皆陰斥去。

translations.literal: Songgotu cultivated the crown prince well, while Mingzhu did the opposite; court officials who attended the crown prince were all secretly driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu cultivated the crown prince; Mingzhu opposed him and secretly drove away officials who served the heir.

sentences.zh: 薦湯斌傅皇太子，即以傾斌。

translations.literal: He recommended Tang Bin to tutor the crown prince, then used this to bring Bin down.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Tang Bin as tutor to the crown prince, then used the appointment to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 會天久不雨，光地所薦講官德格勒明易，上命筮，得夬，因陳小人居鼎鉉，天屯其膏，語斥明珠。

translations.literal: When heaven long withheld rain, Degeli, a lecturer on the Classics whom Guangdi had recommended and who understood the Changes, was ordered to divine; he obtained Guai, and thereupon stated that petty men held the tripods, that heaven hoarded its bounty—the words rebuking Mingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: During a long drought the emperor had Degeli, a lecturer on the Changes recommended by Guangdi, divine; the hexagram Guai led him to declare that petty men held power and heaven withheld its bounty—an indictment of Mingzhu.

sentences.zh: 事具德格勒傳。

translations.literal: The full account is given in the biography of Degeli.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Degeli's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，御史郭琇疏劾：「明珠、國柱背公營私，閣中票擬皆出明珠指麾，輕重任意。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Censor Guo Xiu memorialized in impeachment: 'Mingzhu and Guozhu betray the public for private ends; all draft rescripts in the Grand Secretariat issue from Mingzhu's direction, weight and lightness at his whim.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 (1688) Censor Guo Xiu impeached them: 'Mingzhu and Guozhu betray the public for private gain; Grand Secretariat drafts all follow Mingzhu's orders, light or heavy at his whim.

sentences.zh: 國柱承其風旨，即有舛錯，同官莫敢駁正。

translations.literal: Guozhu carries out his intent; even when there are errors, colleagues dare not correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu carries out his will; even when drafts are wrong, no colleague dares correct them.

sentences.zh: 聖明時有詰責，漫無省改。

translations.literal: Though the sage ruler sometimes rebukes them, they show no reflection or reform.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor sometimes rebukes them, they show no remorse or reform.

sentences.zh: 凡奉諭旨或稱善，明珠則曰'由我力荐'；

translations.literal: Whenever an edict was received or someone was praised, Mingzhu would say, 'Through my strong recommendation';
translations.idiomatic: When an edict praised someone, Mingzhu would say, 'That was my recommendation';

sentences.zh: 或稱不善，明珠則曰'上意不喜，我從容挽救'；

translations.literal: when someone was criticized, Mingzhu would say, 'The emperor's mind was displeased; I calmly rescued the matter';
translations.idiomatic: when someone was criticized, he would say, 'The emperor was displeased, but I smoothed it over';

sentences.zh: 且任意附益，市恩立威，因而要結群心，挾取貨賄。

translations.literal: moreover he arbitrarily added embellishments, traded favors to build prestige, and thereby sought to bind men's hearts and extort bribes.
translations.idiomatic: he embellished at will, traded favors for power, bound followers to him, and extorted bribes.

sentences.zh: 日奏事畢，出中左門，滿、漢部院諸臣拱立以待，密語移時，上意罔不宣露。

translations.literal: Each day when audience was finished he went out through the central left gate; Manchu and Han ministers of the boards and courts stood bowed awaiting him, whispering for long stretches, and nothing of the emperor's mind failed to be disclosed.
translations.idiomatic: After daily audience he left by the central left gate while Manchu and Han ministers waited bowing; he whispered with them at length and revealed the emperor's every intention.

sentences.zh: 部院事稍有關係者，必請命而行。

translations.literal: On any matter of the ministries and courts that bore the slightest relation, they had to ask his leave before acting.
translations.idiomatic: On any ministry matter even remotely connected, they had to seek his permission first.

sentences.zh: 明珠廣結黨羽，滿洲則佛倫、格斯特及其族侄富拉塔、錫珠等，凡會議會推，力為把持；

translations.literal: Mingzhu widely formed a faction: among Manchus, Folun, Gesite, and their clansmen Fularata and Xizhu and others—in every joint conference and recommendation he strove to control the outcome;
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu built a wide faction among the Manchus—Folun, Gesite, Fularata, Xizhu, and others—and controlled every joint conference and recommendation;

sentences.zh: 漢人則國柱為之囊橐，督撫籓臬員缺，國柱等展轉徵賄，必滿欲而後止。

translations.literal: among Han officials Guozhu was his purse; for posts of governor-general, governor, and provincial intendant Guozhu and others passed bribes through intermediaries and would not stop until desires were fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: among Han officials Guozhu handled the money; for governorships and provincial posts they extorted bribes through intermediaries until every demand was met.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年學道報滿應升者，率往論價，缺皆預定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, learning-intendant officials whose terms expired and who were due for promotion generally went to bargain over price; every vacancy was prearranged.
translations.idiomatic: By Kangxi 23, learning-intendants due for promotion routinely bargained for posts; every vacancy was sold in advance.

sentences.zh: 靳輔與明珠交結，初議開下河，以為當任輔，欣然欲行。

translations.literal: Jin Fu was allied with Mingzhu; when the lower river was first proposed to be opened, it was thought Fu should be entrusted with it, and he was eager to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu was allied with Mingzhu; when opening the lower river was first proposed, Fu was eager to take charge.

sentences.zh: 及上欲別任，則以於成龍方沐上眷，舉以應命，而成龍官止按察使，題奏權仍屬輔，此時未有阻撓意也。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to appoint someone else, they nominated Yu Chenglong, who was then enjoying imperial favor, to answer the order; Chenglong's rank was only surveillance commissioner, and the power of memorializing still belonged to Fu—at this time there was as yet no intent to obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wanted another appointee, they nominated the favored Yu Chenglong, though he was only a surveillance commissioner and Fu still controlled memorials—at that point they had not yet meant to obstruct.

sentences.zh: 及輔張大其事，與成龍議不合，乃始一力阻撓。

translations.literal: When Fu magnified the undertaking and could not agree with Chenglong, only then did he use all his strength to obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu inflated the project and clashed with Chenglong, he began to obstruct it with all his power.

sentences.zh: 明珠自知罪戾，對人柔顏甘語，百計款曲，而陰行鷙害，意毒謀險。

translations.literal: Mingzhu knew his own guilt; toward others he showed a gentle face and sweet words, using every device to be ingratiating, yet secretly he acted with ruthless harm—his intent poisonous and his schemes treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his guilt, Mingzhu spoke gently in public and used every wile to please, while secretly he acted with ruthless malice.

sentences.zh: 最忌者言官，惟恐發其奸狀，考選科道，輒與訂約，章奏必使先聞。

translations.literal: He most feared censorial officials, dreading lest they expose his wicked conduct; at the selection of censors and surveillance commissioners he always made agreements with them that memorials must be heard by him first.
translations.idiomatic: He most feared the censors and bound every new appointee to show him memorials before they were submitted.

sentences.zh: 當佛倫為左都御史，見御史李興謙屢疏稱旨，吳震方頗有彈劾，即令借事排陷。

translations.literal: When Folun was left censor-in-chief, seeing that Censor Li Xingqian's repeated memorials matched the emperor's intent and that Wu Zhenfang had made considerable impeachments, he ordered that pretexts be used to bring them down.
translations.idiomatic: As left censor-in-chief, Folun saw Li Xingqian's memorials win praise and Wu Zhenfang's impeachments gain traction, and had them destroyed on trumped-up charges.

sentences.zh: 明珠智術足以彌縫罪惡，又有國柱奸謀附和，負恩亂政。

translations.literal: Mingzhu's craft was enough to cover over his crimes, and with Guozhu's wicked schemes echoing his own, he betrayed grace and threw government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu's cunning covered his crimes; with Guozhu's schemes echoing his, he betrayed the throne and threw government into disorder.

sentences.zh: 伏冀立加嚴譴。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope they may immediately receive severe punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge immediate severe punishment.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，上諭吏部曰：「國家建官分職，必矢志精白，大法小廉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor instructed the Board of Civil Appointments: 'The state establishes offices and divides duties; officials must pledge themselves to purity and integrity, uphold the great law and practice small scruples.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor told the Board of Civil Appointments, 'The state sets up offices and divides duties; officials must pledge themselves to purity, uphold the law, and practice scruple in small things.

sentences.zh: 今在廷諸臣，自大學士以下，惟知互相結引，徇私傾陷。

translations.literal: Now the ministers at court, from grand secretaries downward, know only how to draw one another into factions and favor private ends while undermining rivals.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ministers at court, from grand secretaries down, know only faction-making, private favor, and ruining rivals.

sentences.zh: 凡遇會議，一二倡率於前，眾附和於後，一意詭隨。

translations.literal: Whenever they meet in conference, one or two lead the way at the front and the multitude echoes behind, all of one mind in unprincipled compliance.
translations.idiomatic: In every conference one or two lead and the rest echo, all unprincipled followers.

sentences.zh: 廷議如此，國是何憑？

translations.literal: When court deliberation is like this, on what can the state rely?
translations.idiomatic: When court deliberation is like this, what can the state rely on?

sentences.zh: 至於緊要員缺，特令會同推舉，原期得人，亦欲令被舉者警心滌慮，恐致累及舉者，而貪黷匪類，往往敗露。

translations.literal: As for important vacancies, the special order for joint recommendation was originally meant to obtain the right men and also to make those recommended guard their hearts and cleanse their thoughts, fearing that they might bring down their recommenders—yet corrupt and wicked sorts are often exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Important posts were to be filled by joint recommendation to find worthy men and make appointees fear disgracing their patrons—yet the corrupt are often exposed anyway.

sentences.zh: 此皆植黨納賄所致。

translations.literal: All this comes from planting factions and accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: All this comes from faction-building and bribery.

sentences.zh: 朕不忍加罪大臣，且用兵時有曾著勞績者，免其發覺。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to punish great ministers, and since some rendered merit in time of war, I spare them exposure.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to punish great ministers, and some rendered merit in war, so I spare them exposure.

sentences.zh: 罷明珠大學士，交領侍衛內大臣酌用。」

translations.literal: Remove Mingzhu from the grand secretaryship and hand him over to the senior interior ministers of the guards for appropriate employment.'
translations.idiomatic: Strip Mingzhu of his grand secretaryship and assign him to the senior interior ministers of the guards.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，授內大臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed an interior minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed an interior minister.

sentences.zh: 後從上徵噶爾丹，督西路軍餉，敘功復原級。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor in the campaign against Galdan, supervised western-route army provisions, and on review of merit had his former rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the campaign against Galdan, supervised western-route provisions, and had his rank restored for merit.

sentences.zh: 明珠自罷政後，雖權勢未替，然為內大臣者二十年，竟不復柄用。

translations.literal: From the time Mingzhu left office, though his power and influence did not decline, yet for twenty years as interior minister he never again held the reins of government.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office Mingzhu retained influence, but for twenty years as interior minister he never regained real power.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 47 (1708).

sentences.zh: 子性德、揆敘自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Xingde and Kuixu have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xingde and Kuixu have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 余國柱，字兩石，湖廣大冶人。

translations.literal: Yu Guozhu, style name Liangshi, was a native of Daye in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guozhu, styled Liangshi, was from Daye in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授兗州推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed investigating censor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 9 jinshi, he became investigating censor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷行人司行人，轉戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a courier in the Courier Office and then made a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became a courier in the Courier Office, then a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，考授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he was examined and appointed supervising censor of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 (1676) he became supervising censor of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵，國柱屢疏言籌餉事，語多精覈。

translations.literal: War was then in progress; Guozhu repeatedly memorialized on raising supplies, his language often precise and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: During the wars he memorialized repeatedly on supplies with sharp, precise analysis.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20 (1681) he became vice censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 旋授江寧巡撫，請設機制寬大緞疋。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed governor of Jiangning and asked to establish machine production of wide satin bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Jiangning and proposed machine weaving of wide satin.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「非常用之物，何為勞費？」

translations.literal: He received an edict: 'This is not an article of daily use—why expend labor and expense?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, 'This is not an everyday item—why waste labor and money?'

sentences.zh: 當明珠用事，國柱務罔利以迎合之，及內轉左都御史，遷戶部尚書，湯斌繼國柱撫江蘇；

translations.literal: When Mingzhu held power, Guozhu strove for illicit profit to please him; when he was transferred within the capital to left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of revenue, Tang Bin succeeded Guozhu as governor of Jiangsu;
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzhu's power Guozhu sought illicit profit to please him; promoted to left censor-in-chief and revenue minister, he was succeeded in Jiangsu by Tang Bin;

sentences.zh: 國柱索斌獻明珠金，斌不能應，由是傾之。

translations.literal: Guozhu demanded that Bin present gold to Mingzhu; Bin could not comply, and for this reason they brought him down.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu demanded gold for Mingzhu; when Bin refused, they destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授武英殿大學士，益與明珠結，一時稱為「余秦檜」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, bound himself still closer to Mingzhu, and for a time was called 'Yu Qin Hui.'
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 (1687) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, tightened his bond with Mingzhu, and was nicknamed 'Yu Qin Hui.'

sentences.zh: 會上謁陵，中途召于成龍入對，成龍盡發明珠、國柱等貪私。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to attend the tombs, he summoned Yu Chenglong midway for audience; Chenglong fully exposed the greed and private conduct of Mingzhu, Guozhu, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: While attending the tombs the emperor summoned Yu Chenglong en route; Chenglong fully exposed the corruption of Mingzhu, Guozhu, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 上歸詢高士奇，士奇亦以狀聞。

translations.literal: On his return the emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, who also reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, who confirmed the report.

sentences.zh: 及郭琇疏論劾，言者蜂起，國柱門人陳世安亦具疏糾之，頗中要害，國柱遂奪官。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiu's memorial of impeachment followed, accusers swarmed forth; Guozhu's disciple Chen Shi'an also submitted a memorial of correction that struck vital points, and Guozhu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Xiu's impeachment, accusers swarmed; even Guozhu's disciple Chen Shi'an memorialized against him with telling force, and Guozhu lost his post.

sentences.zh: 既出都，於江寧治第宅，營生計，復為給事中何金蘭所劾，命逐之回籍。

translations.literal: After leaving the capital he built a mansion at Jiangning and managed his livelihood; he was again impeached by Supervising Censor He Jinlan and ordered expelled to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving Beijing he built a mansion at Jiangning; Supervising Censor He Jinlan impeached him again and he was ordered home.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 佛倫，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Folun, of the Sumuru clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Folun of the Sumuru clan was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: From clerk he was promoted step by step to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂既死，其孫世璠猶據滇、黔，命佛倫總理糧餉，通鎮遠運道，旋兼理四川糧餉。

translations.literal: After Wu Sangui died, his grandson Shifan still held Yunnan and Guizhou; Folun was ordered to take general charge of provisions, open the transport route through Zhenyuan, and soon also manage Sichuan provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui's death his grandson Shifan still held Yunnan and Guizhou; Folun was put in charge of provisions, opened the Zhenyuan supply route, and soon managed Sichuan as well.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was transferred to be vice president of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended he became vice president of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左都御史，擢工部尚書，轉刑、戶兩部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to left censor-in-chief, promoted to minister of the Ministry of Works, and then transferred through the Ministries of Justice and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became left censor-in-chief, then minister of works, then served in justice and revenue.

sentences.zh: 先是下河工程，靳輔與按察使於成龍議不​​協，命佛倫偕侍郎熊一瀟等勘議。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the lower-river project, Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong could not agree; Folun was ordered, together with Vice President Xiong Yixiao and others, to survey and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: On the lower-river project Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong clashed; Folun joined Vice President Xiong Yixiao and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 佛倫受明珠指，議如輔言，為總漕慕天顏所劾。

translations.literal: Folun took Mingzhu's direction and decided in accord with Fu's view; he was impeached by Director-General of Grain Transport Mu Tianyan.
translations.idiomatic: Directed by Mingzhu, Folun ruled for Fu's plan and was impeached by Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan.

sentences.zh: 御史陸祖修亦劾佛倫袒輔，且言：「九卿會議時，尚書科爾坤等阿佛倫意，尚書張玉書、左都御史徐乾學言興屯所佔民田應還之民，科爾坤置不聞。

translations.literal: Censor Lu Zuxiu also impeached Folun for favoring Fu, and stated: 'At the conference of the Nine Ministers, Minister Ke'erkun and others toadied to Folun's intent; Ministers Zhang Yushu and Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Qianxue said the civilian fields seized for military colonies should be returned to the people, but Ke'erkun paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Zuxiu also impeached Folun for favoring Fu, saying that at the Nine Ministers' conference Ke'erkun toadied to Folun while Zhang Yushu and Xu Qianxue argued that colony lands should be returned to the people—Ke'erkun ignored them.

sentences.zh: 他九卿或不得見隻字。」

translations.literal: The other ministers sometimes did not see a single character.'
translations.idiomatic: Other ministers sometimes never saw a word of the proceedings.'

sentences.zh: 上怒，下部嚴議。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent the case down for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered a severe inquiry.

sentences.zh: 及郭琇劾明珠，指佛倫為明珠黨，因解佛倫任。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiu impeached Mingzhu and named Folun as of Mingzhu's faction, Folun was accordingly removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xiu impeached Mingzhu and named Folun as his partisan, Folun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 召輔等廷對，佛倫乃奏停屯田，並汰前所設官。

translations.literal: Fu and the others were summoned for court audience; Folun then memorialized to halt the military colonies and also eliminate the offices previously established.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and others were summoned to court; Folun then urged halting the colonies and abolishing the offices created for them.

sentences.zh: 部議奪佛倫官，上命留佐領。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberation stripped Folun of office; the emperor ordered that he retain company command.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended stripping Folun of office; the emperor let him keep company command.

sentences.zh: 旋授內務府總管。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 出為山東巡撫，疏請均賦役，令紳民一體應役，詔嘉其實心任事。

translations.literal: Sent out as governor of Shandong, he memorialized asking to equalize tax and corvée levies and make gentry and commoners alike answer service; an edict praised his earnest devotion to duty.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Shandong he memorialized to equalize taxes and corvée so gentry and commoners alike bore service; the emperor praised his earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 初，濰縣知縣硃敦厚以贓私為巡撫錢鎯所發，乞徐乾學請於鎯，獲免，且內擢主事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei County magistrate Zhu Dunhou had been exposed for corruption by Governor Qian Li; he begged Xu Qianxue to intercede with Li, was spared, and was even promoted within the capital to director.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei County magistrate Zhu Dunhou had been exposed for corruption by Governor Qian Li; through Xu Qianxue's intercession he escaped punishment and was even promoted to director in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 至是事發，下佛倫鞫實，乾學坐奪官。

translations.literal: When the matter now came to light, Folun was ordered to investigate the facts; Qianxue was stripped of office on conviction.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair surfaced, Folun investigated; Qianxue lost his post.

sentences.zh: 佛倫又劾琇知吳江縣時，嘗侵公帑，其父景昌故名爾標，乃明御史黃宗昌奴，坐賊黨誅，琇改父名冒封典，當追奪。

translations.literal: Folun also impeached Xiu, saying that when he was magistrate of Wujiang he had embezzled public funds; his father Jingchang's former name was Erbiao and he had been a slave of Ming censor Huang Zongchang, executed as a rebel partisan; Xiu changed his father's name to usurp ennoblement and posthumous honors, which ought to be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Folun also charged that as Wujiang magistrate Xiu had embezzled public funds, and that his father Jingchang—formerly Erbiao, a slave of the Ming censor Huang Zongchang executed as a rebel—had been given a false name so Xiu could usurp honors, which should be revoked.

sentences.zh: 乾學故附明珠，後相失，或傳琇疏乾學實主之，故佛倫以是報。

translations.literal: Qianxue had formerly attached himself to Mingzhu and later fell out with him; some said Xiu's memorial was really directed by Qianxue, and so Folun repaid him in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue had once sided with Mingzhu and later broke with him; some said Xiu's impeachment was really Qianxue's work, and Folun struck back.

sentences.zh: 尋擢川陝總督，入為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi, then entered the capital as minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi, then minister of rites in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，授文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 (1699) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，琇入覲，訟父受誣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Xiu came to audience and pleaded that his father had been slandered.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 39 (1700) Xiu came to audience and pleaded that his father had been falsely accused.

sentences.zh: 上詰佛倫，自承不實，當奪官，援赦得免。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Folun; he confessed that the charges were untrue, that he ought to be stripped of office, and obtained exemption by appeal to amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Folun; he admitted the charges were false, deserved dismissal, and escaped punishment through amnesty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以原品休致。

translations.literal: Before long he retired at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 論曰：康熙中，滿洲大臣以權位相尚者，惟索額圖、明珠，一時氣勢熏灼，然不能終保令名，卒以貪侈敗。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the Kangxi reign, among Manchu great ministers who vied in power and position, only Songgotu and Mingzhu—for a time their momentum scorched all—yet could not preserve a good name to the end and finally fell through greed and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In the Kangxi era only Songgotu and Mingzhu among Manchu ministers truly vied for power; for a time their influence blazed, yet neither kept a good name and both fell to greed and extravagance.

sentences.zh: 索額圖以附皇太子得罪，禍延於後嗣。

translations.literal: Songgotu offended through attachment to the crown prince, and disaster extended to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu fell for siding with the crown prince, and disaster reached his descendants.

sentences.zh: 明珠與索額圖競權，不附皇太子，雖被彈事罷相，聖祖猶念其贊撤籓，力全之，以視索額圖，豈不幸哉？

translations.literal: Mingzhu contended for power with Songgotu and did not attach himself to the crown prince; though impeached and removed from the premiership, the Kangxi Emperor still remembered his support for abolishing the fiefs and used all his strength to preserve him—compared with Songgotu, was he not fortunate?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu rivaled Songgotu and did not back the crown prince; though impeached and removed from office, the Kangxi Emperor still remembered his support for abolishing the fiefs and protected him—compared with Songgotu, was he not the luckier man?

sentences.zh: 若國柱、佛倫，則權門之疏附矣。

translations.literal: As for Guozhu and Folun, they were merely distant adherents of the power-holders.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu and Folun were only lesser hangers-on of the powerful.
